subject: Realtime stream threshold surge & circuit-breaker guidance for LiveChat integration
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@finexco.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-22T14:12:00Z
Subject: LiveChat stream severe latency spike (started ~14:05 UTC)

Hi Michael —

We started seeing degraded streaming latency in our LiveChat integration around 14:05 UTC. Users are getting long pauses (~8-12s) mid-response and some sessions are dropping back to non-streaming completions. This is affecting three high-traffic accounts (A, B, C).

We attached a short sample log (finexco_stream_logs_20261022.csv). Can you confirm whether this is on your side or something in our client configuration? We pushed a quick client restart but the problem persisted.

We’re in a customer-facing cadence—appreciate an expedited triage and any immediate mitigations we can apply on our side.

—Jordan
Senior PM, FinexCo

Attachments: finexco_stream_logs_20261022.csv

From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@finexco.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-22T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: LiveChat stream severe latency spike (started ~14:05 UTC)

Jordan — thanks for the quick heads-up and logs. I’m escalating this to our Live Runtime team and looping in Vanessa (SE) and Rachel (Support). Initial ask: can you confirm whether you’re using our streaming websocket or HTTP chunking path, and whether you have client-side circuit-breaker/backoff configured?

Immediate actions from our side (we’ll start these now):
- Pull end-to-end traces for your account and edge shard (~14:00–14:45)
- Check for autoscaling or worker-restart events in the region serving your traffic
- Validate model variant fallbacks and circuit-breaker triggers in the routing layer

Short-term mitigation you can apply now (non-disruptive):
1) Turn on client-side niched retry with exponential backoff (start at 250ms, cap 2.5s).
2) If you have a permissive fallback path, set client to accept non-streaming fallback for content-critical sessions only.
3) Reduce max_tokens_per_chunk to 64 for the next hour to lower steady-state token bursts.

We’ll follow up with a triage note in ~45–60 minutes. If this needs a faster escalation to an SLA credits review we can open that thread.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@finexco.com>
Cc: michael_grant@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-22T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: LiveChat stream severe latency spike (started ~14:05 UTC)

Jordan — thanks for the log extract. Quick summary from our runtime inspection:
- Edge shard serving FinexCo experienced an atypical token burst between 14:04:30–14:12:20 UTC that increased per-request queue depth and triggered our backpressure path.
- There were no worker restarts, but one model-variant fallback occurred for a small fraction (~2.1%) of requests which forces non-streaming responses.

I’m attaching a short runbook (runbook_livechat_circuit_breaker.pdf) with conservative client-side settings that we recommend you apply immediately. Key items from the runbook:
- Circuit-breaker: trip if > 3 consecutive stalled streaming frames or if average token-latency > 1.8s for 2 minutes.
- Backoff retries: initial 250ms, multiplier 1.8, max 2500ms. Implement jitter ±200ms.
- Chunking: set tokens_per_chunk = 48–64 for high-concurrency endpoints and fall back to batch responses if > 3 reconnects in 30s.
- Graceful fallback: if circuit-breaker trips, mark session as "degraded-stream" and switch to non-streaming synchronous call for continuity.
- Monitoring: emit a metric stream_latency_buckets and set an alert at P95 > 1.2s for 5m.

Temporary config we can push from our side (if you approve): bump your reserved concurrency on Dedicated pools for the next 2 hours, and enable a lightweight adaptive batching flag for your account so the runtime avoids small inefficient batches.

Let me know if you want me to apply the temporary server-side flags now (I can do a controlled toggle). I’ll stay on the thread for follow-up diagnostics.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Thanks Vanessa — that runbook looks actionable. Please:
1) Apply the adaptive batching toggle and bump reserved concurrency for the next 2 hours.
2) We’ll implement the client changes (backoff + chunk size) now and rotate them in production at 17:00 local time.
3) We’d also like a temporary quota increase to avoid throttling while we stabilize traffic (FinexCo account ID: FX-7721).

Also: could you generate a short incident summary and a set of post-incident follow-ups? Our CS and engineering leads will want a bulletized timeline and recommended durable changes.

Appreciate the quick help.

—Jordan

Jordan — quick recap and action plan following today’s triage:

Timeline (concise):
- 14:04:30 UTC: token-burst begins on serving edge; P95 token latency climbs > 2.0s
- 14:05–14:12 UTC: increased queue depth; some requests fallback to synchronous response
- 14:30 UTC: Redwood toggled adaptive batching for FX-7721 and applied a 2-hour reserved concurrency bump
- 16:11 UTC: FinexCo confirmed they will deploy client backoff + chunk-size change at 17:00 local

Immediate outcomes:
- Short-term client changes + our adaptive batching reduced P95 token latency back under 1.0s for the stabilized window (observed 17:15–17:45).
- We will continue sampling traces to validate steady-state.

Post-incident follow-ups (owner / ETA):
- (Vanessa) Produce full incident postmortem with timeline, RCA, and proposed durable mitigations — ETA 2026-10-25.
- (So0jin) Create an alert runbook entry and update the shared runbook doc with new threshold values — ETA 2026-10-24.
- (Michael) Coordinate the temporary quota increase and any SLA credit requests with FinexCo — on-going; update by 2026-10-23.

Requested from FinexCo: please share any additional client logs or traces around reconnect patterns after 17:00 so we can correlate.

We’ll keep this thread as the single source of truth for customer communications and I’ll post the postmortem link once ready.
